sources: The **National Report** (A/HRC/WG.6/53/TTO/1) was not yet available at the time of assessment.
meta.headline: **No relevant action (C)** is the dominant outcome, with a thin evidence base on the State's own account because its National Report was not yet available (14 recommendations are **D**). **Partial implementation (B)** appears where the documents record concrete measures: the 2023 National Strategic Action Plan on gender-based and sexual violence, anti-trafficking plans, shelters and a first conviction, a National Climate Change Policy, near-universal free education and a comprehensive social protection system. **No relevant action (C)** persists on the mandatory death penalty (48 people under sentence of death in 2026, no moratorium), treaty ratification, refugee legislation, an anti-discrimination law, a national human rights institution and prison conditions. There is a clear regression (**E**): consensual same-sex relations were re-criminalised in 2025 when the Court of Appeal reinstated sections 13 and 16 of the Sexual Offences Act, and repeated States of Emergency since 2024 have expanded police powers.
meta.note: No national report was available for this review when the assessment was made, so more recommendations are graded D (no information).

themes.theme: Human rights education, trainings & awareness raising

blocks.summary: Human rights training for officials
blocks.rationale: Capacity-building for law enforcement and public officials was delivered through UN technical assistance but is project-dependent and not institutionalised.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/TTO/2), para. 10 — United Nations country team: "human rights training remained project-dependent and was not systematically institutionalized"

recommendations.text: Provide human rights education and training for government officials and for law enforcement officers, including through international cooperation with partners

Develop sustainable and human rights-centred training programmes for the police and the judiciary regarding issues such as gender-based violence, human trafficking, migrant smuggling, sexual exploitation and forms of child abuse
Enhance training programmes for judicial and law enforcement officers in the areas of gender-based violence, human trafficking and child abuse
Continue efforts to increase the training of personnel and set up the necessary infrastructure to properly include students with disabilities and children with special needs

blocks.summary: Curb corruption and strengthen transparent procurement
blocks.rationale: The Human Rights Committee welcomed steps to prevent and combat corruption, but the whistle-blower protection bill is delayed and enforcement is weak.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/TTO/2), para. 9 — Human Rights Committee: "welcomed the steps taken to prevent and combat corruption among persons exercising public functions"
UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/TTO/2), para. 9 — Human Rights Committee: "delays in adopting the whistle-blower protection bill"

recommendations.text: Take concrete actions to curb corruption by creating transparent public procurement processes at all levels of government and investigating police officers who take or solicit bribes

blocks.summary: Climate policy and participation
blocks.rationale: Trinidad and Tobago adopted a National Climate Change Policy, submitted its second NDC and strengthened disaster preparedness; participation of marginalised groups remains limited.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/TTO/2), para. 37 — United Nations country team: "the adoption of the National Climate Change Policy, the submission of the second nationally determined contribution and strengthened disaster preparedness"
UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/TTO/2), para. 37 — United Nations country team: "the limited participation of marginalized groups"

recommendations.text: Continue to implement policies to mitigate the effects of climate change and strengthen the resilience of communities from a human rights approach
Ensure the meaningful participation of women, children, persons with disabilities and local communities in the development and implementation of climate change and disaster risk reduction frameworks
Maintain its commitment to advocating for climate action that is consistent with existing human rights agreements, obligations, standards and principles
Adopt and implement measures to adequately protect the population against the risks of natural disasters, inevitable due to climate change
Continue to implement effective climate change and disaster risk reduction policies, and advocate for climate action by all nations

blocks.summary: Combat violent crime while respecting rights
blocks.rationale: Violent crime remains high; repeated States of Emergency since 2024 have expanded police powers and are reported not to be yielding results.

Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/TTO/3), para. 4 — JS4: "State of Emergency had been repeatedly in effect"

recommendations.text: Continue to combat violent crimes to ensure the safety of the people

blocks.summary: Improve prison conditions and reduce pretrial detention
blocks.rationale: Conditions remain inadequate despite ongoing reforms; most prison infrastructure projects remain unfinished and remand detention is prolonged; a 2026 Parole Bill has been introduced.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/TTO/2), para. 18 — Human Rights Committee: "despite ongoing reforms, detention conditions remained inadequate"

UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/TTO/2), para. 18 — United Nations country team: "the 2026 Parole Bill sought to introduce an early release system"

recommendations.text: Adopt comprehensive public policies aimed at guaranteeing the rights of persons deprived of liberty and eliminate overcrowding in prisons
Take further measures to improve prison infrastructure and the system for determining the security classification of inmates

Continue to improve conditions for prisoners and persons awaiting trial by further investing in infrastructure, training personnel and taking actions such as expanding judicial discretion to reduce bail terms and amounts for people accused of petty offences

blocks.summary: Reform the criminal justice and penitentiary system

Carry out the necessary reforms to the judicial and penitentiary system, in order to resolve the problem of prison overcrowding and improve conditions of detention

themes.theme: Human trafficking & contemporary forms of slavery

Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/TTO/3), para. 15 — ECLJ: "the first conviction secured under the Trafficking in Persons Act"

Intensify efforts to combat trafficking in persons and forced labour

blocks.summary: Strengthen health services including HIV/AIDS

Take all necessary measures to fight against discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity

blocks.rationale: Sexual orientation and gender identity are still not protected grounds; the Equal Opportunity Act amendment has been pending for over a decade.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/TTO/2), para. 50 — ILO Committee of Experts: "the proposed inclusion of sexual orientation as a protected ground in the Equal Opportunity Act had remained pending for over a decade"

recommendations.text: Take further steps to combat all forms of violence, abuse and discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity
Take the necessary steps to combat discrimination and violence against women and children and on the basis of sexual orientation and gender identity

blocks.summary: Adopt the national gender policy and the national strategic action plan
blocks.rationale: The National Strategic Action Plan on gender-based and sexual violence 2023-2027 was approved by Cabinet; the status of a national gender policy is not reported and CEDAW notes delays in adopting gender equality frameworks.
evidence: Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/TTO/3), para. 27 — JS2: "in 2023, the Cabinet approved a National Strategic Action Plan"

recommendations.text: Adopt the national gender policy and the national strategic action plan to end sexual and gender-based violence to ensure that gender-based violence is prioritized and receives increased budgetary allocation to implement communication campaigns addressing negative social norms and special measures to prevent sexual and gender-based violence against all women, girls, men and boys, regardless of their legal or migratory status, nationality, gender identity or sexual orientation

blocks.summary: Protect women from violence and strengthen services
blocks.rationale: Specialised police mechanisms, a central GBV registry and the Domestic Violence Act exist; underreporting, resource constraints and weak protection-order enforcement persist.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/TTO/2), para. 39 — United Nations country team: "specialized mechanisms within the police service and the launch of the Central Registry on Gender-based Violence (Umbono System)"
UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/TTO/2), para. 43 — Human Rights Committee: "emergency protection orders reportedly could not be granted to persons of the same sex as the perpetrator"

recommendations.text: Prioritize access to shelters, medical services, legal aid and counselling services for women exiting domestic violence situations
Strengthen measures to combat violence against women by creating specialized police units to investigate these crimes and mitigate impunity
Continue the efforts made to fight against violence and discrimination against women, including by abolishing the law criminalizing the voluntary termination of pregnancy
Continue the efforts to ensure full and effective implementation of the Domestic Violence (Amendment) Act, 2020
Continue the efforts to combat violence against women and girls, establish gender equality and support women’s empowerment

blocks.summary: Promote gender parity and women's empowerment
blocks.rationale: Women's representation increased in government, local government, the judiciary and law enforcement (including the first woman Police Commissioner); women remain under-represented in senior decision-making.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/TTO/2), para. 42 — Human Rights Committee: "welcomed the measures to increase the representation of women in political life"
Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/TTO/3), para. 30 — ICAAD: "the appointment of the first female Commissioner of Police"

recommendations.text: Continue consolidating the achievements made in the promotion of the rights and well-being of women through the National Policy on Gender and Development
Continue with efforts to promote gender parity and enhance women’s participation in the political, economic and social spheres
Continue to strengthen measures to facilitate the economic empowerment of women, especially those in rural areas

blocks.summary: Prevent and eliminate child labour
blocks.rationale: The list of hazardous work prohibited to children has been pending since 2004.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/TTO/2), para. 46 — ILO Committee of Experts: "to ensure the adoption in the very near future of the list of hazardous types of work prohibited to children under 18 years of age"

recommendations.text: Enhance measures to prevent and eliminate child labour, including the involvement of children in hazardous work
Continue the efforts exerted to prevent and eliminate child labour and to prevent the involvement of children in hazardous work

blocks.summary: Prohibit child marriage and eliminate child labour
blocks.rationale: The ILO Committee of Experts urges adoption of the list of hazardous work for children, pending since 2004; the minimum marriage age was raised to 18.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/TTO/2), para. 46 — ILO Committee of Experts: "to ensure the adoption in the very near future of the list of hazardous types of work prohibited to children under 18 years of age"

recommendations.text: Develop and implement legislation that prohibits child marriage

blocks.summary: Promote infrastructure and rural development
blocks.rationale: The documents contain no information on this recommendation.

recommendations.text: Continue to promote infrastructure construction and accelerate the development of rural areas

blocks.summary: Child protection legislation and policy
blocks.rationale: The Human Rights Committee notes efforts to abolish child marriage, raise the minimum marriage age to 18 and prohibit corporal punishment in schools; the national child policy implementation plan is not reported.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/TTO/2), para. 45 — Human Rights Committee: "noting efforts to abolish child marriage, raise the minimum marriage age to 18 and prohibit the corporal punishment of children in schools"

recommendations.text: Continue working on the harmonization and adoption of national legislation towards full compliance with its obligations under the Convention on the Rights of the Child
Continue the momentum towards full compliance with its obligations under the Convention on the Rights of the Child
Continue the efforts exerted to protect and promote the rights of the child and to provide care, protection and rehabilitation for child victims of violence

blocks.summary: Adopt the national child policy
blocks.rationale: The documents contain no information on the national child policy or its implementation plan.

recommendations.text: Deepen the progress made in child protection through the rapid adoption of its national child policy
Urgently adopt the implementation plan for 2020–2030 of the white paper on the national child policy

blocks.summary: Implement the Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights
blocks.rationale: The documents contain no information on this recommendation.

recommendations.text: Continue advancing in the implementation of the Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights through the adoption of a national plan on the matter

blocks.summary: Abolish the death penalty or establish a moratorium
blocks.rationale: The mandatory death penalty for murder and treason remains, courts continue to impose death sentences, 48 people were under sentence of death in 2026 and the State told the Human Rights Committee it did not plan to consider a moratorium until violent crime was under control.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/TTO/2), para. 15 — Human Rights Committee: "the death penalty remained mandatory for murder, leading to a large number of persons on death row"
Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/TTO/3), para. 9 — JS2: "domestic law retained the mandatory death penalty for murder and treason and that 48 individuals were under sentence of death as of 2026"

UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/TTO/2), para. 15 — Human Rights Committee: "the State did not plan to consider abolishing the death penalty or even establishing an official moratorium until violent crime was under control"

recommendations.text: Establish a moratorium on the death penalty with a view to its abolition
Continue to refrain from applying the death penalty and impose an official moratorium on the death penalty
Initiate a process for a State review and discussion of the relevance of the death penalty to Trinidad and Tobago, with a view to considering its complete abolition
Establish a moratorium on the death penalty and consider its abolition and replacement by an alternative penalty that is fair, proportional and in accordance with international standards
Pursue efforts towards the full and unequivocal abolition of the death penalty
Take the necessary steps to move towards the abolition of the death penalty and consider introducing a formal moratorium on its application
Take steps to abolish the death penalty
Develop awareness-raising campaigns concerning the absence of deterrent effects on the application of the death penalty
Repeal provisions allowing for the imposition of the death penalty as the mandatory punishment for some offences and replace them with an alternative sentencing framework

themes.theme: Persons with disabilities: definition, general principles

blocks.summary: Adopt disability legislation
blocks.rationale: A persons-with-disabilities bill and national strategy are still 'under development'; no comprehensive disability law exists.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/TTO/2), para. 48 — United Nations country team: "a persons with disabilities bill and a comprehensive national strategy were under development"
UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/TTO/2), para. 47 — Committee on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities: "the apparent absence of comprehensive disability legislation"

recommendations.text: Adopt domestic legislation to reflect the provisions and principles of the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities and amend all legislation that discriminates against persons with disabilities
Align its domestic legislation with the principles of the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities
Proceed with consideration of strengthening the legal framework for the protection of the rights of persons with disabilities

Accelerate its efforts to develop domestic policies and legislation to protect the rights of persons with disabilities, including through the newly established interministerial committee to oversee the implementation of the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities
Continue the efforts to enable persons with disabilities to secure jobs in the public and private sectors

Maintain efforts, through the interministerial committee, to develop policies and legislation to protect the rights of persons with disabilities in order to address the lack of legislation and to achieve the implementation of the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities
Continue improvements on the protection of people with disabilities, both in its legal framework and in social assistance, and the provision of resources to improve accessibility in all areas

Adopt legislation to reflect the provisions and principles of the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities and consider amending all legislation that discriminates against persons with disabilities (Bulgaria).

blocks.summary: Harmonise the Immigration Act and end pretrial custody of migrants
blocks.rationale: Discriminatory immigration provisions remain and irregular entrants are detained without clear limits.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/TTO/2), para. 14 — Human Rights Committee: "discriminatory provisions in immigration law"

recommendations.text: Take all necessary steps to end instances of individuals being remanded in pretrial custody or immigration detention for extended periods

Expedite legislative processes to harmonize the Immigration Act with international human rights standards and develop an asylum act to ensure the full protection of refugees and asylum seekers, in accordance with international standards

blocks.summary: Adopt a comprehensive definition of discrimination against women
blocks.rationale: CEDAW identifies shortcomings in the definition of discrimination against women; no amendment is reported.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/TTO/2), para. 38 — Committee on the Elimination of Discrimination against Women: "shortcomings in the definition of discrimination against women"

recommendations.text: Adopt a comprehensive definition of discrimination against women in its national legislation in line with the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women

blocks.summary: Enact refugee legislation and an asylum procedure
blocks.rationale: There is still no refugee legislation or status-determination procedure; a High Court ruling declared the Refugee Convention inapplicable (2023); an updated refugee policy and a 2026 Migration Registration Framework offer only partial progress.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/TTO/2), para. 53 — Human Rights Committee: "the absence of a comprehensive legislative and institutional framework for the protection of refugees and asylum-seekers"
UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/TTO/2), para. 52 — United Nations experts: "the High Court ruling declaring the Convention relating to the Status of Refugees inapplicable in Trinidad and Tobago"

UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/TTO/2), para. 51 — United Nations country team: "progress on the regularization of and school access for migrants, refugees and asylum-seekers following an updated refugee policy"

recommendations.text: Enact legislation for the protection of refugees and the granting of asylum under international refugee instruments
Adopt a legislative framework relating to refugees facilitating their protection and integration
Align national legislation on refugees and asylum seekers to international obligations and improve efforts to address human trafficking

Consider adopting additional legal and policy measures to comply with the 1951 Convention relating to the Status of Refugees and its 1967 Protocol, with a view to preventing cases of detention and/or refoulement of asylum seekers
Incorporate the 1951 Convention on the Status of Refugees into national law

Develop an effective legal framework at the national level in compliance with international norms and standards to ensure protection and safeguards for asylum seekers, including by providing adequate reception conditions

recommendations.by: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
recommendations.text: Implement a road map to accelerate the development of national refugee legislation to incorporate international commitments into domestic law
Set up a national refugee status determination procedure in accordance with the relevant provisions of the 1951 Convention relating to the Status of Refugees

Develop national legislation on refugees that is in line with existing international standards and, in the interim, implement the existing national policy on asylum and refugees by addressing smuggling and trafficking and putting in place a refugee determination system (Canada).

blocks.summary: Protect asylum-seekers and migrants
blocks.rationale: No refugee legislation exists; UN experts warned of deportations and the Human Rights Committee of harmful detention practices.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/TTO/2), para. 53 — Human Rights Committee: "increasing numbers of deportations of individuals seeking international protection and harmful detention practices affecting adults and children"

recommendations.text: Ensure the rights granted to asylum seekers and refugees under international refugee conventions by the development of national legislation

Adopt the necessary measures to guarantee the effective protection of migrants, asylum seekers or those who require international protection, ensuring that the principle of non-refoulement and their access to health and education services is observed
